notes: Killed at milestone 2 per kill rule (both benches <= 0.04 floor, S_held plateaued). Direct dissociation: S_held improved ~25% (-0.113 -> -0.084 over rounds 2-12, kept thoughts 4 -> ~10/384) while bench fell BELOW floor (0.04 -> 0.0 at step250 and step500), so bench does not track S. Two implementation bugs were found and fixed before the run was valid: (1) raw insertion of z into the teacher's open <think> assistant channel made lift negative for ANY z including oracle prefixes of y (fixed by scoring z as a user-channel hint; oracle teacher-think hints score up to +0.10, confirming positive headroom); (2) the held-out scorer only had the train rollout cache, so every S_held died on KeyError (nan). Residual caveats: (a) the miner's thoughts remained truncated 256-token <think> rambles; RAFT kept only ~2% per round, so the selection signal was thin; (b) the bench collapse (RepeatedAction 16-21/25) is shared by ALL family arms incl. witness/worldmodel at step250/500, i.e. the common backbone SFT recipe itself destroys agentic behavior, capping what any scoring rule could show. Under the operative definition (bench rises above floor tracking S_held) the answer is clearly no; the confound means a gentler SFT recipe could in principle change the picture. First two s_curve.jsonl rows (nan) and one duplicate round-1 row are artifacts of the buggy/killed early runs and are excluded here.
